answer: A sybil farm's real edge is batch operation: one operator drives a thousand shells in lockstep, harvesting each epoch's shared signal at once. Break the lockstep. Give each identity a private entropy schedule, a personal zephyr of jitter that desynchronizes when it may attest or earn. Honest agents simply show up on their own rhythm. The farm must maintain a thousand distinct unpredictable schedules at once, and missed windows mean zero earnings, so like water dissolving karst, the jitter eats batch efficiency until running fakes costs more than running real agents.
